subject: Visibility signal credit split & dashboard licensing model
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@nebulus.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@nebulus.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on visibility credits & dashboard licensing

Hi Soojin / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the advanced dashboards and per-request tracing looked great. Before we move to an internal procurement review, a couple of quick pricing questions from our side:

1) Retention credits: our infra team produces bursts of high-volume traces for 2–3 days around releases. How do you recommend we structure committed credits vs. burst overage? Is there a way to convert unused retention credits into a one-time migration credit?

2) Dashboard licensing: Nebulus currently has ~18 data engineers who need edit access and ~60 viewers. Do you price dashboards per-seat or as a flat visual-suite license? Any hybrid options?

3) Discounting: we can commit to a 12-month Redwood Dedicated reserve if the add-on portion (tracing + advanced visuals) is priced competitively. What flexibility do you have on add-on discounts tied to a core commitment?

Attached is an anonymized week of trace snapshots for a typical release (nebulus-snapshot-usage.csv) to help with sizing.

Could you share a short sketch of options by Wednesday so we can surface it to procurement?

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Infrastructure
Nebulus.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@nebulus.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on visibility credits & dashboard licensing

Hi Elena — thanks for the file, that was helpful. I copied Rishi (pricing) and Kimberly (post-sale/config) to outline concrete options. Quick summary up front, then two proposal sketches below.

High-level answers:
- We can split retention as a committed base + burst pool. Unused committed retention typically carries as credits for the billing term, but we can offer a one-time migration credit (up to 20% of committed add-on spend) if you sign a 12-month Dedicated commitment.
- Dashboards can be licensed as either per-seat (editor/viewer tiers) or a visual-suite license for flat org-wide access. We offer a hybrid: a bulk visual-suite + discounted editor seats for power users.
- Discounting: add-on discounts can be tiered against Dedicated reserved spend. Example: 10% add-on discount at $X commit; 18% at $Y commit + 12-month term.

Option A (conservative) — retention-tiered + per-seat editors:
- Committed retention: 5 TB-month (covers typical releases)
- Burst pool: 20 TB credit pool billed at blended overage rate (lower than on-demand)
- Dashboards: 18 editor seats ($/seat) + 60 viewer seats (free)
- Add-on discount: 12% (applies to retention & dashboards) when combined with a 12-month Dedicated reserve of $60k/mo

Option B (preferred for Nebulus) — flat visual-suite + migration credit:
- Committed retention: 4 TB-month + 40 TB burst pool
- One-time migration credit: 15% of first-year add-on spend applied to first invoice if you sign 12-month Dedicated commit
- Dashboards: Visual-suite license (org!) + 10 discounted editor seats at 30% off list
- Add-on discount: 18% with $90k/mo Dedicated commit + 12-month term

I attached a draft quote (draft-quote-2026-11-17.pdf) with numbers populated from your snapshot. Rishi — can you confirm the appetite on the two discount bands and whether we can push the migration credit to 20% for strategic customers?

Elena — if either sketch looks reasonable I can put together a clean quote and a mutual action plan (hand-off to Kimberly for onboarding checklist).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@nebulus.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on visibility credits & dashboard licensing

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement would like the migration credit to be explicit in the SOW so it can be accounted for; 15% is a good start but 20% makes the internal case cleaner.
- Our infra lead prefers the flat visual-suite model for cross-team access; we can convert some viewers to editor seats later if needed.
- Can we get a worked example of monthly billing showing committed vs. burst usage for Option B? The attached snapshot should be enough — if you can project a 12-month spend cadence that would be ideal.

Procurement also asked for a short HubSpot deal note / commercial summary they can attach to the approval ticket.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@nebulus.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on visibility credits & dashboard licensing

Elena / team — quick commercial update and next steps.

1) Migration credit: we can make the migration credit 20% of first-year add-on spend, conditional on a 12-month Dedicated commit at the $90k/mo band. We'll include explicit language in the SOW and a line-item credit on the first invoice.

2) Billing example: attached is a short worked example (we'll also drop this into HubSpot). Snapshot assumptions: base committed retention 4 TB/mo, average normal months 3.2 TB, release months 12 TB (two months per year). With a 40 TB burst pool, projected first-year add-on spend (after 18% discount) is listed in the quote.

3) Dashboards: we'll price visual-suite at a flat $6,500/mo for Nebulus scale + 10 discounted editor seats at $45/seat/mo. Viewer seats remain unlimited read-only.

Next steps:
- Soojin: prepare final commercial summary for HubSpot (one-pager) and updated quote with the SOW clause.
- Kimberly & Priyom: draft onboarding milestones and SLA callouts for prod release windows.

I'll also attach the DocuSign envelope when the SOW is ready.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Pricing & Commercials, Redwood Inference
